title: Revoked consent between review and release suppresses the approved send
risk: An operator approval is treated as overriding the consent check, so a customer who opted out an hour ago receives the approved campaign.
preconditions: Namespace gov-apv-<case_id>-<worker_id>; approval queue seeded from fixtures/offline/governance.json.
Operator identities and roles resolved from the fixture operator registry; every decision goes through POST /api/v1/approvals/{id}/decision, the only approval route.
cust-a holds EMAIL marketing consent granted at review time; the campaign targets only cust-a in this scenario.

steps.expected: Status becomes APPROVED and the task is queued for dispatch.

steps.action: Revoke cust-a EMAIL marketing consent before dispatch runs
steps.expected: The consent record becomes revoked with a revocation timestamp.
The send is suppressed at dispatch; the EMAIL adapter counter stays at 0 and the recipient is recorded as suppressed.

steps.action: Read the approval and suppression records
steps.expected: The approval remains APPROVED and records the reviewer, while the execution records the suppression with the consent snapshot - approval and consent are independent controls.

assertions: Human approval never substitutes for consent: the suppressed action produces zero external sends.
The suppression is attributed to the specific recipient and channel, not only to the campaign.
The approval record is not rewritten to rejected; the two controls are recorded separately and both are auditable.
The campaign can still be dispatched to any other recipient who holds a valid grant, so the block is scoped, not global.
forbidden: Treating an operator approval as consent.
Dropping the entire campaign because one recipient lost consent.
Retrying the suppressed recipient in a loop.
evidence: Execution suppression record with the consent snapshot and recipient.
Adapter counter log for the EMAIL channel.
cleanup: Restore the cust-a consent fixture row and delete gov- approval and execution rows.
automation: Real consent evaluation at dispatch time and real approval persistence under test; the channel adapter is the substituted boundary with a per-recipient counter.
note: Generated acceptance specification. Plain specification, not an executable test; no application runtime exists, so the status is NOT_RUN.
